title: PPE — Personal Protective Equipment
blurb: What PPE is, why it is the last line of defence, and how to check, use and replace it.
siteNotes: What PPE is issued for each department and where it is kept
Who to report damaged, worn out or missing PPE to
Which tasks need cut-resistant gloves, chemical gloves or eye protection
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-39 (the venue's 10-minute trainer). Taught as written.

CHECK: the trainer says PPE is the last line of defence after reducing the hazard. This matches the hierarchy of controls and the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992 (employer provides PPE free where risks remain). Please confirm the venue provides PPE free of charge.

CHECK: the trainer lists non-slip footwear as PPE. Slip-resistant footwear is often provided as PPE in hospitality, but whether it counts as PPE depends on whether the employer requires it for the work; please confirm the venue's position.

cards.title: PPE — Personal Protective Equipment
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain why PPE is the last line of defence
- check your PPE before you use it
- report PPE that is damaged, worn out or missing

cards.title: Gear that protects you
cards.body: PPE, Personal Protective Equipment, is the gear that protects you from a hazard.

cards.title: Hazard first, PPE second
cards.body: It is important to understand that PPE is the LAST line of defence. We always try to remove or reduce a hazard first. PPE is there to protect you from what is left.

items.title: PPE
items.text: Protects you from what is left.

cards.title: Right kit for the task
cards.body: PPE only works if you use it, and use it correctly, for the task it is meant for. When the job calls for it, it is not an optional extra.

items.title: Cut-resistant gloves
items.text: For certain knife or slicer tasks.

items.title: Eye protection
items.text: Where there is a splash risk.

cards.title: Before you use it
cards.body: Give your PPE a quick check. Damaged gloves with holes, or a mask that does not fit, will not protect you. Ill-fitting or worn-out PPE gives a false sense of safety, which is almost worse than none at all.

cards.title: Report, do not make do
cards.body: If your PPE is damaged, worn out or missing, report it so it can be replaced. Do not carry on without it. PPE supports safe working. It does not replace it.

left.title: Do
items: Wear it as instructed for the task

right.title: Do not
items: Treat it as a replacement for safe working

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- PPE is the last line of defence
- Use the right PPE, correctly, for the task
- Check it is clean, in good condition and the right size
- Report PPE that is damaged, worn out or missing
- PPE supports safe working, it does not replace it

cards.q: PPE is the LAST line of defence, after reducing the hazard.
cards.why: We always try to remove or reduce a hazard first. PPE protects you from what is left.

cards.q: Which of these is an example of PPE?
options: A name badge on a lanyard
cards.why: Gloves, aprons, eye protection, cut-resistant gloves and non-slip footwear are all PPE.

cards.q: You should check PPE is clean, in good condition and the right size before use.
cards.why: Damaged or ill-fitting PPE will not protect you properly.

cards.q: Damaged or missing PPE should be…
cards.why: Report it so it can be replaced. Do not carry on without it or make do.

cards.q: PPE replaces the need for safe working practices.
cards.why: PPE supports safe working. It does not replace it.

cards.q: Why is ill-fitting or worn-out PPE a problem?
options: It looks untidy to the guests
It gives a false sense of safety
It takes longer to put on each time
It costs more to wash and replace
cards.why: It will not protect you properly, and a false sense of safety is almost worse than no PPE at all.
Cut-resistant gloves are for certain knife or slicer tasks.

cards.q: You should wear PPE as instructed for the task.
cards.why: When the job calls for PPE, it is not an optional extra.

cards.q: Which item of PPE helps prevent slips?
cards.why: Non-slip footwear is PPE that helps prevent slips.
